summary: The marketing team is in execution mode on the Asia Star and Intelligent China program promotions while managing a distracting Outlook lockout and finalizing the Knowledge website redesign.
summaryDetail: The top priority is advancing the Asia Star and Intelligent China program promotions, with Joseph tasked to analyze participant profiles and draft SEO/AI-search visibility prompts, and the team to complete the Intelligent China webpage and launch content. This week, the team must resolve an Outlook account lockout by updating credentials across all devices and confirming the backend unlock with CKGSB, while Joseph and Julie schedule a working session to finalize Knowledge website design feedback. The Knowledge redesign will largely keep the current design but incorporate Joseph's editorial-style layout to surface more articles and indices (BCI, BSI), with videos dispersed by topic and no stock-market ticker. Upcoming priorities include evaluating Berkeley as a possible third program, promoting Andrea and Katya's spotlight videos on LinkedIn and other platforms, and coordinating with SwissCham on the 2026 Sino-Swiss Economic Forum.

decisions.text: Re-login and update passwords on all devices to prevent repeated account lockouts.
Keep the current Knowledge design largely as-is rather than a full revamp, with menu categorization as the main change.
Remove the standalone videos section; disperse videos by topic across the site instead.
Use Joseph's editorial-style layout as inspiration to display more articles and bring indices (BCI, BSI) to the Knowledge homepage.
Do not add a stock-market ticker at the top of the homepage.
Keep the school menu at top and discuss whether the knowledge menu should be centered or left-aligned.
Prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China as the top two programs to promote; put US partnerships (Stanford, Columbia) on hold initially.
